key_insight: PixelSmile enables fine-grained, continuously controllable facial expression editing by disentangling overlapping expression semantics through a fully symmetric joint-training diffusion framework and training on a new continuous-affect dataset.
problem_solved: Overcomes intrinsic semantic overlap and lack of continuous annotations/benchmarks that previously limited precise, identity-preserving facial expression editing and fair evaluation of controllability and structural confusion.
method: Construct FFE: a Flex Facial Expression dataset with continuous affective annotations and publish FFE-Bench to measure structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and expression–identity trade-offs.
Design PixelSmile: a diffusion-based model that uses fully symmetric joint training to disentangle expression semantics, enabling fine-grained, linearly controllable edits while preserving identity.

Evaluate and optimize the trade-off between editing accuracy and identity preservation with dedicated metrics (structural confusion matrix, accuracy, controllability curves, and identity loss analyses).
impact: Provides practitioners with a method and standardized data/bench to perform precise, controllable facial expression edits for applications like avatar animation, reenactment, and data augmentation, while improving reproducible evaluation of expression models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of PixelSmile showing input image → symmetric joint-trained diffusion encoder/decoder → disentangled expression latent → controlled edit → output image.
Continuous affect space visualization (2D scatter/heatmap) from FFE to illustrate dense annotation and semantic overlaps.
Benchmark charts: confusion matrix for structural overlap, accuracy bars, and a trade-off curve plotting editing strength vs identity preservation.
Before/after grid or interactive slider examples showing gradual linear control of expressions on the same identity.
paper_title: PixelSmile: Toward Fine-Grained Facial Expression Editing
paper_authors: Jiabin Hua, Hengyuan Xu, Aojie Li, Wei Cheng, Gang Yu
